run.question:
Alertmanager alert PrometheusNotConnectedToAlertmanagers (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus since 2026-11-15T04:51:32Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert is a true positive about Prometheus's own alerting path: the rule PrometheusNotConnectedToAlertmanagers in the Prometheus rule ConfigMap requires max_over_time(prometheus_notifications_alertmanagers_discovered{job="prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus",namespace="prometheus"}[5m]) < 1 for 10m, i.e. the scraped series stayed at zero discovered Alertmanagers. Nothing in the cluster can be that Alertmanager: across all namespaces there is no Alertmanager StatefulSet, no Alertmanager pod, no Alertmanager Deployment, no Alertmanager Service or Endpoints, and no alertmanager-named ConfigMap; the only monitoring components present are the Prometheus operator, kube-state-metrics, node-exporter and the single Prometheus pod. So Prometheus has no endpoint to connect to, which matches a metric value of 0. The Prometheus pod itself was running and ready with 0 restarts (started 2026-11-15T04:51:00Z on node i-0bc0544469bfef13a, StatefulSet revision unchanged), so this is not a crash of the monitoring pod. What remains unverified is the declared configuration: the generated Prometheus config lives in a Secret that cannot be read, Prometheus/operator container logs returned zero lines, and this metric store contains no prometheus_* or kube_* series, so I could not confirm whether alerting.alertmanagers is empty or points at a now-missing address, nor when/why the Alertmanager disappeared.

claims.text: The rule that opened this investigation is present in ConfigMap prometheus/prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-rulefiles-0 (file prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-ac4fa589-...yaml): alert PrometheusNotConnectedToAlertmanagers, expr max_over_time(prometheus_notifications_alertmanagers_discovered{job="prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus",namespace="prometheus"}[5m]) < 1, for: 10m, severity: warning. A firing instance therefore means the scraped series stayed below 1 (zero discovered Alertmanagers) for 10 minutes.

No Alertmanager workload exists anywhere in the cluster: the cluster-wide StatefulSet list contained 6 objects (chi-clickhouse-main-0-0, jaeger-traces-recorder, prometheus-alert-recorder, topology-monitor, opensearch-cluster-master, prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus) and none is an Alertmanager; the cluster-wide Deployment list contained 36 objects and none is an Alertmanager.

No Alertmanager pod exists in any namespace: a cluster-wide pod query matching names containing 'alertmanager|prometheus' returned 9 pods (8 in namespace prometheus plus data-recorders/prometheus-alert-recorder-0) and none is an Alertmanager server; the namespace prometheus pod list likewise contains only the operator, kube-state-metrics, prometheus-...-0 and five node-exporter pods.

Namespace prometheus has no Alertmanager Service and no Alertmanager Endpoints: Services are prometheus-kube-prometheus-operator, prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus, prometheus-kube-state-metrics, prometheus-operated and prometheus-prometheus-node-exporter; the matching Endpoints objects are the same five (ports 10250, 9090/8080, 8080, 9090, 9100). No 'alertmanager-operated' service/endpoints object exists.

Namespace prometheus holds only two ConfigMaps: kube-root-ca.crt and prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-rulefiles-0 (keys include the kube-prometheus prometheus/operator/kubernetes-apps rule files plus otel-demo alerting and workload-recording rules). There is no Alertmanager configuration ConfigMap in that namespace.

The Prometheus pod prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0 is Running, all containers ready, restartCount 0, started 2026-11-15T04:51:00Z (32s before the alert's start) on node i-0bc0544469bfef13a; its owning StatefulSet prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus was created 2026-11-14T05:37:32Z, is ready 1/1 and its currentRevision equals updateRevision (prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-677d847d59).

The Prometheus container runs with --config.file=/etc/prometheus/config_out/prometheus.env.yaml rendered by config-reloader from /etc/prometheus/config/prometheus.yaml.gz, where the 'config' volume is a Secret whose name is redacted in the pod spec, and the only ConfigMap volume is the rule files (prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-rulefiles-0). No Alertmanager config or alertmanager-related volume appears in the pod spec.

No event in the cluster references this Prometheus pod or any Alertmanager: a cluster-wide event query filtered on node i-0bc0544469bfef13a / Evict / OOM / NodeNotReady / Reboot / Killing / prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus returned only 5 unrelated events (data-recorders pods scheduled 04:58-04:59, clickhouse-unified-recorder stopping 05:02, product-catalog and recommendation containers stopping 05:15); the returned event data only spans from 2026-11-15T04:58:52Z onward.

Primary hypothesis: Prometheus is not connected to any Alertmanager because its alerting configuration has no Alertmanager endpoint at all — the kube-prometheus-stack Alertmanager is not deployed in this cluster (no StatefulSet, Pod, Deployment, Service, Endpoints or alertmanager config object in any namespace), so prometheus_notifications_alertmanagers_discovered stays 0 and the 10m rule fires. This is consistent with every cluster object checked, but the Prometheus CR's spec.alerting.alertmanagers field could not be read to confirm it is empty.

Alternative candidate that remains open: the Prometheus alerting configuration still names an Alertmanager endpoint (for example a previously existing alertmanager-operated service) but that object is gone, so discovery returns 0 or sends fail. This cannot be checked here because the generated config is inside the unreadable 'config' Secret, no Prometheus/Alertmanager config ConfigMap exists, and the Prometheus container logs returned no lines in either the current or previous instance.

Rejected: that a Prometheus container crash, OOMKill or eviction broke the notification path. The pod is Running with both containers ready and restartCount 0, no OOMKilled/Evicted or node event involving it was returned, and its StatefulSet revision is unchanged; the 04:51:00Z pod start therefore reflects a pod (re)creation whose reason is not visible, not a crash loop.

gaps: The generated Prometheus configuration is stored in the pod's 'config' Secret (name redacted); Secrets cannot be read in this Run, so I could not verify whether spec.alerting.alertmanagers is empty or names a now-missing address, nor which Alertmanager was configured before the incident.

Prometheus/operator/alert-recorder container logs were unavailable: fetch_pod_logs for prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0 (with and without a filter) and for prometheus-kube-prometheus-operator-57d68989cc-hkbnh and data-recorders/prometheus-alert-recorder-0 read 0 lines from all current and previous streams, so no 'no alertmanagers'/DNS/connection-refused log evidence exists for this Run.

The queried Prometheus store has no prometheus_* metric names (get_metric_names for prometheus_.* and .*alertmanager.* returned nothing) and get_series for prometheus_notifications_alertmanagers_discovered returned nothing, so the actual 0 value of the series is inferred from the firing alert, not read directly.

kube-state-metrics series are not in this store either: get_metric_names for kube_.* returned nothing and only traces_span_metrics_calls_total was returned when probing traces_span_metrics_calls_total|http_server_request_duration_seconds_count|kube_pod_container_info, so I could not check historical series to see whether an Alertmanager pod existed earlier in the window.

Change history is not integrated (not_integrated: change_history) and cluster events only start at 2026-11-15T04:58:52Z, so why the Prometheus pod was created at 04:51:00Z and whether an Alertmanager workload was deleted earlier (which would explain a for:10m alert firing at 04:51:32Z) cannot be established.

Kubernetes custom resources (monitoring.coreos.com Prometheus and Alertmanager) are not among the readable kinds, so the declared Alertmanager CR / alerting config could not be inspected; an empty networkpolicy result was not citable, so network-level blocking was neither confirmed nor excluded by evidence.

Not checked: whether alert delivery for other alerts was affected in the window, and whether any otel-demo application service showed its own error or latency impact; no impact on those services is claimed here.
next_steps: Read the kube-prometheus-stack Helm values / Prometheus CR and the alerting config Secret in namespace prometheus to confirm whether alertmanager.enabled is false or spec.alerting.alertmanagers is empty or stale (requires a principal that may read Secrets and monitoring.coreos.com CRs).

If Alertmanager is intended to exist, deploy/restore it (Alertmanager CR, alertmanager-operated Service, alertmanager-config Secret) and re-check the Prometheus /api/v1/alertmanagers endpoint and prometheus_notifications_alertmanagers_discovered on 100.96.5.74:9090, since this metric store does not carry Prometheus self-metrics.

Establish why the Prometheus pod was recreated at 2026-11-15T04:51:00Z (audit log or kubelet/node records, as cluster events before 04:58:52Z are gone) and re-check Kubernetes object state around that time for an Alertmanager StatefulSet/Service removal.

Verify whether the alert that opened this investigation was delivered by an Alertmanager outside this cluster; if so, confirm that this Prometheus's alerting config intentionally points at that external endpoint and that the target is reachable.
